title: Channelized entrypoints and route contracts (work-in-progress)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects thinking, sketches, and backlog grooming notes for a multi-channel console navigation redesign. Focus: define entrypoint channels (left rail, compact top nav, command palette, deep links/task cards), establish route contracts that guarantee minimal surface semantics for integrations and backstage services, and propose a phased rollout with telemetry gates and route deprecation policies.

High-level problem statement (short):
- Current console navigation is monolithic: heavy left rail + multiple ad-hoc deep links.
- Integrations (deployments, rollouts, metrics, cost views) rely on brittle route assumptions.
- Mobile/compact modes, and product-embedded SDKs, need consistent entry semantics.

Goals:
1) Create explicit channel definitions and surface guarantees for each (what state is preserved, which query params are allowed).
2) Reduce route churn for 3rd-party links and internal bookmarks by introducing stable route contracts and migration redirects.
3) Improve discoverability of task-focused flows (e.g., create deployment, start rollout, inspect model metrics) via channelized entry cards.
4) Support keyboard-first and deep-link scenarios without duplicating UI surfaces.

Channel definitions (proposed):
- Channel: LeftRail (primary workspace navigation)
  - Contract: canonical tree hierarchy, supports hierarchical selection and context bread crumbs. Preserves session-scoped route: workspaceId, projectId, activePane.
  - Allowed params: workspaceId, projectId, modelId, view, anchor.
  - Not allowed: ephemeral eval IDs (should be routed through ephemeral route).

- Channel: Quickbar (command palette / omnibox)
  - Contract: ephemeral (non-persistent) navigation; performs intent-level transitions (open/create/inspect) and can focus nested modals. Returns to last LeftRail context on dismiss.
  - Allowed params: intent, targetId, focusPath.

- Channel: DeepLink (external links / email / SDK)
  - Contract: stable public contract. Must tolerate missing resources (redirect to list view + toast) and always record source=deeplink for telemetry.
  - Allowed params: canonicalResourceId, highlight, source.

- Channel: TaskCard (launcher surface)
  - Contract: contextual entry with prefilled intent (e.g., start rollout with pinned model). If prerequisites missing, show guided setup.

Wireframe notes (text sketches):
1) LeftRail condensed: three vertical zones—(A) workspace selector (compact chip), (B) channel groups (Models, Deployments, Monitoring, Billing, Settings), (C) quick actions (Create, +). Hover expands to full labels; click pins expanded state.
2) Compact topnav (mobile / narrow width): a single row with workspace name, search/quickbar, and overflow menu. Deep-linkable path breadcrumbs appear as chips under topnav when in a nested view.
3) Quickbar overlay: center-floating, 1-line command input, results in two columns: fuzzy results + contextual quick actions. Example command: "deploy model:x to staging" previews required fields inline before routing to full create flow.
4) TaskCard modal pattern: cards surfaced in dashboard and left rail quick actions; clicking opens a preflight modal that can be confirmed or expanded to full page.

Backlog grooming (prioritized rough):
- CONS-908 Define route contract spec and registry (owner: Aisha) — 3 pts — acceptance: spec doc, unit tests for route normalizer, 1 example redirect rule.
- CONS-912 Implement stable deeplink handler + fallback UI (owner: Evan) — 5 pts — acceptance: deeplink handler with source tagging, one integration test with broken resource fallback.
- CONS-915 LeftRail condensed prototype (owner: Priya) — 8 pts — acceptance: interactive prototype in storybook, keyboard nav support, a11y review notes.
- CONS-919 Quickbar UX + intent parser (owner: Liam) — 13 pts — acceptance: basic intent parser (open/create/inspect), telemetry events wired.
- CONS-924 TaskCard surface and preflight modal (owner: Sofia) — 5 pts — acceptance: task card component, modal flow, backend stub for prefill.
- CONS-930 Routing telemetry and SLOs for rollouts (owner: SRE lead) — 5 pts — acceptance: dashboards for redirect rate, broken deeplink ratio < 1% after rollout.

Grooming notes / acceptance criteria details:
- Route contracts must be documented in a machine-readable registry (yaml/json) and validated by a small middleware library (route-normalizer).
- All redirects from deprecated routes must return 301-like behaviour within client routing semantics and emit a "route_migration" event.
- DeepLink handler must set cookie/localStorage to remember the intended channel if user signs in mid-flow.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): ship route contract spec + route-normalizer libs to canary team. Manual testing of 10 critical links.
- Phase 1 (beta opt-in): left rail condensed and quickbar UI behind feature flag for 20% of orgs. Collect UX metrics (task completion time, quickbar usage, left rail pin rate).
- Phase 2 (public rollout): enable Quickbar by default, switch deeplink handling to new contract; enable client-side redirects for deprecated routes. Monitor broken-deeplink ratio gate (<1%).
- Phase 3 (cleanup): remove old route handlers, publish migration guide for integrators.

Telemetry & success metrics (initial):
- quickbar-invocation-rate (per-session) target: 0.3+ within 7 days of rollout.
- deeplink-fallback-rate target: < 2% in beta, <1% in public.
- average-route-resolution-latency < 50ms for in-client routing operations.
- percent-of-users-with-pin-state-preserved across sessions > 95%.

Edge cases & open questions:
- Q: How to handle cross-workspace deeplinks when user has access to multiple workspaces? Suggestion: surface chooser modal after auth; preserve original intent.
- Q: Should Quickbar mutate URL when invoking ephemeral actions? Pros: shareable; Cons: noisy history. Current recommendation: do not modify browser history for ephemeral Quickbar results; use history.replace for focusable states.
- Edge: bookmark for ephemeral evals — solution: require generation of share token and exchange via deep link.

Accessibility considerations (short):
- All channel entry points must have ARIA labels and keyboard access (LeftRail: arrow keys; Quickbar: Cmd/Ctrl+K; Task Cards: Enter/Space).
- Contrast checks on condensed rail hover previews.

Design/engineering handoffs (next steps):
- UX: produce high-fidelity frames for left-rail collapsed/expanded states and Quickbar results. (Owner: Priya)
- Eng: create route-normalizer library and a small middleware that enforces allowed params (Owner: Evan).
- SRE: define dashboards and set alert on broken-deeplink ratio (Owner: SRE).
- PM: schedule alpha by 2025-02-01, beta by 2025-03-15.

Unresolved items to record in the backlog:
- Decision on URL mutation policy for Quickbar (CONS-937).
- DeepLink auth flow when 3rd-party embed denies cookies (CONS-941).
- Migration naming convention: stableResourceId vs resourceSlug (CONS-949).

Notes to reviewers:
- Please call out any hard dependencies on existing route aliases in your area (search, billing, dedicated UI).
- If you maintain any public integrations that hardcode routes, flag them in linked_artifacts.

Scratchpad / loose ideas (do not block on these):
- Use a small "route-level feature flag" header in responses to help debug client redirects.
- Experiment: Quickbar suggestions could be surfaced as ephemeral TaskCards on mobile for one-tap flow.
- Consider route versioning: /v1/deployments/:id -> /deployments/:id?v=2025-03 to allow safe server-side changes.

Relevant links / refs (copied from Slack & PRs):
- Slack thread: #cons-navigation "deeplink failures with billing links" (link above)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1294 (quickbar prototype)
- Linear tickets: CONS-908, CONS-912, CONS-915, CONS-919

-- end of doc --

Notes to self: push spec to Confluence in "Console Entrypoints Strategy" space, cut a short RFC and route contract registry before next grooming.
